title: The AFO musicians' cooperative and its bitterness
summary: Matassa views the AFO of Harold Battiste and Red Tyler as a great idea that lost focus on blackness, and says they were cheated by a black man.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: It shouldn't be said about that as we move along. Um, let's see. Another, another group of people, and I wanted to get your input or your opinion of, of the organization, was the formation of AFO in 1960, 61. I mean, Harold Batiste, Red Tyler.

Oh, okay. There was one of those cases where I, I could be sympathetic to everything they, they, they felt, including some bitterness to whites. Mm-hmm. And, and, and, you know, you might say with a lot of justification, in fact. Okay. So, so, so, so I, I think I, I, I was able to be, while not part of their inner circle of, as such, I, I could be their, their friend and their, and that kind of stuff and, and work with them and, and try to help and that kind of stuff. But my, my question is, did, what, how did you perceive their organization, the concept of.
